text:
ryan.s: Hey team — FinEdge POC needs outbound allowlist for the Dedicated endpoint. They want a short sandbox (2 weeks) and legal asked about data residency + certs. Can we run through options?
mira.k: Quick Q — are they okay with us giving them static egress IPs from our Dedicated pool or do they need private VPC peering?
ryan.s: They prefer not to open peering yet. Ops asked for a set of IPs to allowlist. Security's legal wants to confirm we don't retain traffic logs tied to their customer IDs for the POC.
eva.ops: We can issue ephemeral static EIPs for a POC Dedicated pool but it's an add-on and needs a ticket to provisioning. Typical lead time ~48h. IPs will be stable for the POC window but rotate if we reprovision.
jamie.sec: From security side: two items — 1) we need to confirm TLS in transit + server certs (we provide), 2) they asked about mTLS for mutual auth. Dedicated endpoints support API key by default; mTLS is only available on Private/VPC installs. I'll flag legal: we can provide SOC2 report and pointer to our data retention policy.
alex.p: Also raise pricing: ephemeral static-egress is a $X/day add-on for Dedicated POCs (we include baseline in the quote). If they want guaranteed SLA + fixed IP long term, suggest Dedicated Reserved + egress subscription.
ryan.s: Good — what exact info do I need from customer to get provisioning started?
mira.k: Ask for 1) customer network contact (email + off-hours contact), 2) allowlist CIDR they will accept (or confirm single IPs), 3) expected peak RPS / avg token throughput so we size the pool, 4) billing contact + PO for the egress addon if needed, 5) any legal constraints (no cross-border egress) so we pin region.
eva.ops: Also ask if they will be routing through their proxy — if so we support outbound proxying but they must open our egress on their proxy and provide TLS intercept exceptions for api.redwood.ai endpoints.
jamie.sec: For the security questionnaire: I can prefill these sections — encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+), data-at-rest encryption, KMS options on Private, audit logs availability on Dedicated/Private. If they need pentest or architecture diagrams attachable to the SQA, ping me and I'll attach the certs and compliance pack.
ryan.s: Perfect. I'll send them an email template. Anything I should include verbatim?
mira.k: Include this snippet so their infra team can test reachability quickly:
```
# quick curl test (POC token placeholder)
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer POC_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"ping"}'
```
ryan.s: Nice. Will do. Also they asked if we can rotate IPs mid-POC — how disruptive?
eva.ops: Rotation requires a short window where IPs change; if they only allow a single IP then we'd need to schedule a maintenance window and update the allowlist. If they can accept a small CIDR (e.g., /29) it's smoother.
jamie.sec: Note: if they require absolute non-rotation, recommend Private deployment. We can offer a temporary Private sandbox but that has higher onboarding time and legal approvals.
alex.p: Sales note — include an explicit line item in the quote: "POC static egress (2 weeks)" and list the cost and provisioning ETA. That avoids surprise chargebacks.
ryan.s: Ok drafting email now. I'll request network contact + allowed CIDR + peak tokens + PO for egress. I'll also attach the compliance doc Jamie mentioned.
ryan.s: @deploy-bot can you open a provisioning ticket for a 2-week static-egress for account finedge-0001 once I drop the PO number here?
deploy-bot: Ticket created: PROV-4821 — Dedicated POC static egress request for finedge-0001. ETA 48h. Assigned to eva.ops.
eva.ops: Got it. Once the PO is attached we'll queue the EIPs. I'll document IPs here and ping when ready.
jamie.sec: I'll draft the SQA attachments and share before you send. Leave me one hour. :thumbsup:
ryan.s: Thanks team — looping in FinEdge now. I'll post updates in this thread.
